The tea ☕

The two things people actually argue about

Both are things she's addressed herself, on the record. Here's the public timeline, and what the chart's pattern lines up with — not proof of anything, just a lens.

📱 The trolling she called out publicly
What's public

From around 2014 onward she was repeatedly blamed online whenever Virat Kohli had a bad match, and separately trolled over her own films and choices.

She's spoken about it directly in multiple interviews — calling it out as harassment, not fair criticism, and has been vocal about the mental-health toll of pile-ons aimed at public figures' families.

What the chart hints

The loudest stretch of this — 2017 through mid-2019 — falls inside her Jupiter–Rahu antardasha. Rahu is the classic "sudden, oversized, uncontrollable public attention" planet.

Read as a pattern, not a cause: outsized visibility with an equally outsized downside, arriving together.

🎬 "Did she quit acting?"
What's public

Tabloids spent 2019–2023 running some version of "Anushka Sharma has quit films" while she had no releases.

She's corrected this repeatedly and specifically: it was a deliberate choice to prioritise production, a newborn, then a second child — not a career in decline.

What the chart hints

That entire gap sits inside her Saturn mahadasha — the planet of boundaries, patience and doing things at your own pace, not the crowd's.

A Saturn era reads as "sets its own timeline" far more naturally than it reads as "faded out."

Being straight with you: none of the above is the chart explaining or excusing anything that happened in her life — astrology can only offer a pattern to look at after the fact. The facts are public record; the astrological reading is interpretation, offered for context, not verdicts.

Astrology, but make it make sense

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second someone was born — her janam kundli, in the Hindi term for it. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology treats that snapshot as the raw material you were handed — not fate, your starting kit.

Hers: 1 May 1988, Ayodhya. That sky had the Sun and Mars both at their strongest possible sign, and Venus sitting on its own home turf. Three placements do most of the talking.
LESSON 02

The planets, and what each one runs

Nine of them. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, different room.

  • Exalted — the planet's classical best-case sign. As strong as that planet ever gets.
  • Own sign — the planet owns the place outright. Full strength, no permission needed.
  • Everywhere else — a guest. Functional, not special.
Her scorecard: two planets exalted (Sun, Mars) and one on its own sign (Venus) — three strong placements in one chart. Most people get zero. She got three, which is closer to main-character casting than average.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the part most people have never heard of, and it's the most useful.

Your planets don't all act at once. They take turns running your life, for years at a stretch. Vedic astrology calls a planet's turn a dasha. Whoever's turn it is colours that whole chapter.

Her turns, computed:
Rahu 1988–2003 · Jupiter 2003–2019 · Saturn 2019–2038 (current) · Mercury 2038–2055

Her entire film career from debut to comeback runs across just two mahadashas: Jupiter carried the rise, Saturn is carrying the step-back-and-return.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

A 16- or 19-year turn is too blunt to be useful on its own, so each one splits into shorter stretches run by the other planets. That's where the year-to-year story lives.

Inside her chart:
Jupiter–Mercury (2008) → the debut
Jupiter–Mars (2016) → Pink, under her other exalted planet
Jupiter–Rahu (2017–19) → the wedding, and the loudest trolling
Saturn–Saturn (2019–22) → motherhood, stepping back
Saturn–Mercury (2022–25) → second child, the acting return
Saturn–Venus (2026–29) → running right now
LESSON 06

The one placement that isn't settled: Mercury

Everything above is solid because it only needs the date and place of birth — which are public. But we ran an hour-by-hour scan of her entire birth day anyway, the same way we check for any close call.

Mercury sits in Aries from midnight until roughly 6:33 PM IST, then crosses into Taurus for the rest of the day. Every other planet in her chart holds its sign for the full 24 hours — Mercury is the single exception.

Since Aries covers about 18.5 of the day's 24 hours, we treat Mercury in Aries as her primary, majority-of-day placement everywhere on this page. If she was born after roughly 6:33 in the evening, her Mercury is in Taurus instead — we don't know which, because no birth time for her has ever been published.
LESSON 07

What we genuinely can't tell you

Here's where most celebrity astrology sites quietly cheat, and we won't.

There are two halves to a chart. Which sign each planet is in — that only needs the date, so everything above is solid. And the houses, which need the exact minute of birth.

No birth time for Anushka Sharma has ever been published. AstroSage — usually the first stop for this — shows a placeholder chart that even miscomputes from the wrong city. We ran her chart across the full 24 hours instead: every other placement holds, but the rising sign would land on a different one of all 12 signs depending on the hour.

So on this page you will not see us say "her 7th house of marriage" or "her career house" — that would be a guess dressed as fact. Other sites will. Ask them which birth time they used.
LESSON 08

So — is Anushka Sharma manglik?

One of the most-searched questions about her, and the honest answer is the same one every no-birth-time chart runs into.

"Manglik" (mangal dosha) depends on which house Mars sits in relative to the lagna — and houses need the birth time. Without it, this cannot be honestly answered either way, and neither can whether any dosha would be cancelled.

What we can say: her Mars is exalted in Capricorn — about as strong as Mars gets, sign-wise. Whether that lands in a manglik house is unknowable without her exact birth minute. Any source giving you a confident yes, no, or a specific remedy/gemstone for her chart has picked a birth time and isn't telling you which one.

FAQ 01

What is Anushka Sharma's birth time?

No verified birth time has ever been published for her. AstroSage's own listing is an unrated placeholder that miscomputes from the wrong city, so this page publishes only what her birth date settles honestly — zodiac signs, nakshatra and dasha eras — and never houses or lagna.

FAQ 02

What is her zodiac sign and nakshatra?

By Vedic (sidereal) reckoning her Moon sits in Libra, in the Swati nakshatra. Her Sun-side placements put the Sun exalted in Aries alongside Mercury and Jupiter. The full birth chart is above — every position computed, not copied from anywhere.

FAQ 03

Is Anushka Sharma manglik?

It can't be honestly answered without a verified birth time, because mangal dosha is a house-level question. What's solid: her Mars is exalted in Capricorn. Whether that placement falls in a manglik house — or whether any dosha it created would be cancelled — depends on an exact birth minute nobody has published.

FAQ 04

Do Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli's kundlis match?

Real 36-guna Milan matching needs a verified birth time for both people, and neither has one published. What we can compare honestly are Moon signs and nakshatras — her Libra Moon in Swati against his own chart, which you can see on his Virat Kohli kundli page. A proper compatibility read needs your own birth details, not a celebrity guess.
